Episode 08 · The deep canyon

THE PRESSURE VAULT

A research pod should be sinking toward a sealed vault. Instead it is drifting up, and its ballast display insists nothing has changed. One of the instruments is wrong.

BuoyancyArchimedes’ principlePressure in liquidsNet forceGrades 9–12
CHAPTER 1

CHAPTER 01 · THE MISSION

Does deeper water push up harder?

NEREID-8 is a rigid pod, completely under water. On the way down, the water pressure on its hull grew with every meter. Predict before you calculate: as the pod went deeper, what happened to the buoyant force on it, the upward push of the water?

CHAPTER 02 · THE WARNING

What is lifting the pod?

The flowmeter says the ballast tank holds only 100 kg of seawater, not the 180 kg on the display. First, the idea: what sets the size of the buoyant force on NEREID-8?

Now measure the forces

Find the buoyant force on NEREID-8. Then find the net force on it with the real 100 kg of ballast, and say which way it points.

Seawater density ρ1,025 kg/m³
Pod volume V (rigid hull)2.40 m³
Pod mass, tank empty2,320 kg
Ballast now (flowmeter)100 kg
FB = ρ g V  (the weight of the displaced seawater)  ·  W = (mpod + mballast) g  ·  g = 9.81 m/s²
Net force = the bigger force minus the smaller one. It points the way the bigger force points.

CHAPTER 03 · YOUR PHYSICS

Can the hull take the vault?

The vault door is 42.0 m below the surface. The cabin stays at normal air pressure, so what loads the hull is the gauge pressure of the water: its pressure above normal air pressure. NEREID-8’s hull is rated for 450 kPa, and the team keeps 20 kPa in reserve, so its working limit is 430 kPa. Find the gauge pressure at the vault door. Then find the force the water puts on the cockpit dome, which covers an opening of 1.50 m².

Depth of the vault door h42.0 m
Seawater density ρ1,025 kg/m³
Dome opening, area A1.50 m²
Hull working limit430 kPa
p = ρ g h  (gauge pressure at depth h)  ·  1 kPa = 1,000 Pa  ·  g = 9.81 m/s²
F = p A  (force on an area A)  ·  1 kN = 1,000 N
CHAPTER 04 · CHOOSE THE FILL

How much water goes back in?

The leak is shut, and Maya can let seawater back into the ballast tank. The sight glass has three marks. The dive computer approves a descent only if the net force on the pod is downward and no more than 500 N. That is the most the vertical thrusters can hold, so the pod can stop at the vault door; below the door, the canyon drops past the hull’s working depth. You choose the fill.

CHAPTER 04 · THE OUTCOME

MAYA · SYSTEMS ENGINEER
CHAPTER 05 · BRING THE CORE HOME

Load the core

The vault’s rack holds 90 kg of cores, and the mission needs at least 60 kg of them. Every kilogram of core in the basket makes NEREID-8 heavier, so ballast water has to come out to keep the pod hovering: the net force must stay within 100 N of zero. And there is a safety rule: if the pumps fail, blowing the ballast tank empty must lift the pod, core and all, with at least 600 N. Choose a core load and a ballast setting that pass all three limits.

Buoyant force FB24,132.6 N
Pod mass, tank empty2,320 kg
Hover: net forcewithin 100 N
Emergency lift≥ 600 N
W = (mpod + mcore + mballast) g  ·  net force = FB − W  (upward if positive)
Emergency lift, tank blown empty = FB − (mpod + mcore) g
Limits: core load ≥ 60 kg  ·  net force within 100 N of zero  ·  emergency lift ≥ 600 N
1 · Largest core load2 · Approved design
